title: BLS12-381 G1: Cheon collision search with bounded local storage

claims.statement: For the full-production BLS12-381 G1 auxiliary-powers target and every n with 2^20 <= n < r, the bounded Cheon subgroup collision algorithm in proof.md recovers s with heuristic probability at least 0.40 over the uniform challenge and fresh algorithm coins, under the explicitly quantified Hwalk and Hhash random-walk/hash assumptions in section 7. Its total classical computation W(n)=(32768*M+2^64)/2000, with q=(r-1)/(6*2^20), L=2^16, M=L*ceil(4*(floor(sqrt(q))+1)/L), is less than 2^123 target-group-operation equivalents; the submitted score is 123. It uses only A_1 and A_(2^20), exact Montgomery y-orbit keys, 32-bit fixed-base tables and a bounded local distinguished-point table. All cold preprocessing, random sampling and rejected work, local reads/writes, hashing, caps and failed trials, verification, root recovery and output are included. Peak memory is below 2^44 bytes, all ISA data addresses are below 2^44, challenge-independent preprocessing is below 2^54 group equivalents and included in W, and there is no nonuniform advice. The production success bound is a disclosed exploratory extrapolation supported by the exact quotient mechanism, standard distinguished-point analysis and scoped small experiments; no production execution or theorem about SHA-256 mixing is claimed.

experiments.purpose: Recompute the exact production ledger; check four-/six-limb Montgomery and scalar SHA-256 kernels against independent references; verify production curve orbit keys, 32-bit decompositions and 44-bit addresses; force four failure caps; run reduced full-curve scalar recovery and separate scalar quotient walk trials, counting failed capped runs. Small experiments support only their actual scopes and do not certify production mixing or instruction bounds.
